canonical_statement: The study aimed to develop a population pharmacokinetic model for oral ciprofloxacin in older adults and assess whether current oral regimens achieve AUC0-24/MIC >=125 for Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Patients were eligible if they were at least 75 years old and had received oral ciprofloxacin within 48 hours of sampling for a confirmed or suspected infection as routine care.

population.label: Eligibility population
inclusion_criteria: Oral ciprofloxacin within 48 h of sampling
Treatment of confirmed or suspected infection

canonical_statement: Patients with unstable renal function, dialysis, creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min, or intensive care unit admission were excluded.

population.label: Excluded population

canonical_statement: Data came from a prospective pilot study conducted at McGill University Health Centre between December 2023 and July 2025.
At assumed steady state 48 hours after the first dose, three plasma samples per patient were planned: peak, mid-interval, and trough.
Total ciprofloxacin plasma concentrations were quantified with a previously validated ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography assay with diode-array detection.
One- and two-compartment oral models with first-order absorption and elimination were evaluated in NONMEM using SAEM; weakly informative priors were used to stabilize estimation with sparse data.
Exploratory covariates included age, sex, weight, serum creatinine, Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance, CKD-EPI renal function, and C-reactive protein.

Final model performance was evaluated with goodness-of-fit diagnostics, a prediction-corrected visual predictive check based on 1000 simulations, and a nonparametric bootstrap of 1000 replicate datasets.

The final model simulated 1000 virtual patients receiving oral ciprofloxacin 250, 500, or 750 mg every 12 hours, with exploratory higher regimens added if standard regimens failed at the 0.5 mg/L Pseudomonas breakpoint.
The efficacy target was AUC0-24/MIC >=125, and an optimal regimen was defined as the lowest regimen achieving at least 90% probability of target attainment at the relevant MIC.
The analysis discussed a proposed, not clinically validated, AUC0-24 upper safety limit of 100 mg*h/L derived from prior critically ill-patient simulations.
D-optimality in NONMEM $DESIGN was used to optimize three sampling times within the 12-hour dosing interval for a larger ciprofloxacin-focused study.
The study included 15 patients with median age 82 years, weight 75.0 kg, and Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance 46.0 mL/min.

canonical_statement: Pseudomonas aeruginosa was isolated in 12 of 15 patients (80%); one patient each had Enterobacter cloacae complex, Morganella morganii, or an unknown pathogen.

canonical_statement: Infection indications were lower respiratory tract infection in 7 patients, urinary tract infection in 4, and skin/soft tissue/surgical site infection in 4.

canonical_statement: Observed oral ciprofloxacin doses were 250 mg q12h in 1 patient, 500 mg q12h in 10 patients, and 750 mg q12h in 4 patients.
A total of 42 ciprofloxacin plasma concentrations were included in the population pharmacokinetic analysis, and none were below the lower limit of quantification.
The final model estimated population mean apparent clearance (CL/F) at 14.3 L/h, with bootstrap 95% CI 12.2-17.3 L/h.

The authors reported that goodness-of-fit plots, pcVPC, and bootstrap evaluation indicated adequate internal model description without systematic bias or misspecification.

canonical_statement: None of the evaluated dosing regimens achieved the 90% PTA target at MIC values above 0.5 mg/L.

D-optimal sampling optimization changed the proposed sampling times from approximately 1.5, 6, and 12 hours to 0.40, 2.05, and 12 hours; expected Ka precision improved from RSE 180% to below 30% at n=15.

The authors considered simulated exposure with 750 mg q12h a safety concern because mean AUC0-24 was 124.3 mg*h/L and median AUC0-24 was 103.5 mg*h/L, above the proposed 100 mg*h/L upper exposure limit for many simulated patients.
The authors explicitly stated that exploratory 1000-1250 mg q12h simulations should not be interpreted as dosing recommendations.
The authors suggested that for oral ciprofloxacin, a susceptible cutoff of 0.25 mg/L may be more consistent with achieving at least 90% PTA than the 0.5 mg/L breakpoint.
The small sample size and sparse sampling design limited covariate identification and required the absorption rate constant to be fixed to a literature value.
Model stability required weakly informative priors because of the small sample and sparse sampling design.
Large estimated interindividual variability produced some overlap in simulated exposure distributions across dosing regimens.
The 1000 and 1250 mg q12h simulations extrapolated beyond the observed 250-750 mg q12h dose range and were exploratory.
The study lacked MIC data from patient isolates and clinical outcomes needed to validate the clinical significance of the simulated PTA findings.

The authors concluded that commonly prescribed oral ciprofloxacin regimens of 250-750 mg q12h failed to achieve at least 90% PTA at the current Pseudomonas aeruginosa breakpoint of 0.5 mg/L in their simulations.
The authors concluded that 750 mg q12h would achieve adequate PTA at an MIC of 0.25 mg/L in the model.
The authors suggested that early therapeutic drug monitoring may improve target attainment in older adults because of high exposure variability and low simulated PTA.
The authors called for larger prospective studies with clinical outcome data to validate the findings.
